official.deadline_central_display: 1 February 2027 (Erasmus School of Economics 2027-2028 round; application window opens 1 December 2026, closes 31 January 2027 23:59)
official.deadline_note: There is no university-wide scholarship deadline: each participating school sets its own, and the central EUR pages currently list the 2026-2027 round as closed with 2027-2028 information expected in autumn 2026. ESE has published the 2027-2028 Erasmus Trustfonds window (1 December 2026 - 1 February 2027, decisions by 13 March 2027). Historically ESSB, ESHCC, ESPhil and ESL used a 1 April scholarship deadline with the programme application due 15 March (ESSB/ESHCC) and decisions by 1 May (ESHCC/ESL) or before 1 June (ESSB).
official.status_note: The central Erasmus Trustfonds pages state the 2026-2027 application round is closed (deadline passed) with 2027-2028 information to follow in autumn 2026. Erasmus School of Economics has already published its 2027-2028 Trustfonds round: applications open 1 December 2026 and close 1 February 2027 (deadline 31 January 23:59), with all applicants informed by 13 March 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Central page: '€17.500 for housing, living costs and statutory fee.' ESE 2027-2028 breakdown: the tuition fee is waived for students paying either the statutory fee (EUR 2.695) or the institutional fee (EUR 21.000 for non-EEA; EUR 2.695 waived through the scholarship and the residual EUR 18.305 paid by the school). ESHCC wording: '€17.500 for housing, living costs, and tuition fees.' TSH Changemaker variant: covers the statutory tuition fee.
benefits: €17.500 for housing, living costs and statutory fee, granted for one academic year (maximum, central Erasmus Trustfonds page)

ESE 2027-2028 package: full tuition fee waiver (statutory EUR 2.695 or institutional EUR 21.000 for non-EEA), living allowance of €1.200 per month (€14.400 for one academic year), a one-off personal allowance of €249, and the €228 immigration fee waived if applicable

Combined Erasmus Trustfonds-TSH Changemaker Scholarship: €9.895 for living costs and statutory tuition fee plus one year free-of-charge accommodation in a Social Hub residence (monthly living allowance of €600)
ESSB and EMC: an additional fee waiver covering the difference between the institutional fee and the statutory fee for candidates who pay the institutional fee
ESL: a tuition fee waiver by Erasmus School of Law is made available alongside the scholarship (Trustfonds and Ter Kulve scholarships)
eligibility: Central requirement (Erasmus Trustfonds Scholarship): you are planning to start a master programme at Erasmus University Rotterdam, you are considered a high achieving student, and you are unable to finance your study yourself

ESE 2027-2028: full-time first-year master students from EEA and non-EEA countries, never previously enrolled as a full-degree master student in the Netherlands, admitted to Master Accounting, Auditing and Control, Master Econometrics and Management Science, or Master Economics and Business
Academic threshold: average final bachelor result of at least 7.50 (ESE) or 8.0 (ESSB, ESHCC, EMC, ESL) on the Dutch grading scale of 1 to 10
ESHCC 2026-2027 round: EEA national applying for a full-time English-taught master programme at ESHCC
EMC 2026-2027 round: non-EEA nationals applying for the full-time research masters Health Sciences, Neuroscience or Molecular Medicine

TSH Changemaker variant: unconditionally admitted at the start of the programme and belonging to one or more disadvantaged or underrepresented groups (e.g. limited financial, educational, social or health resources; refugee or newcomer status; ethnic or religious marginalisation; disability; first-generation student; LGBTQI+ identity with potential safety risks), with demonstrated community involvement

Ter Kulve Scholarship (ESL): nationality on the World Bank income classification, recent relevant work experience after the bachelor, and a commitment to return to the home country; one scholarship available
requirements: Register for the master programme in Studielink and submit the application documents in the EUR Admissions Portal before the scholarship deadline (ESSB: before 15 March; ESE: before 1 February 2027)

Be enrolled no later than 1 September (ESSB/ESE) of the academic year for which the scholarship is requested; an admission offer is not required at the moment of application at ESE, but only applicants with an admission offer are considered

ESE: the immigration application must be completed by 10 July; scholarship applicants are instructed to submit their immigration application by May at the latest, including the tuition fee, the living-cost deposit and the IND handling fee
Only one type of scholarship will be awarded to one applicant: you may apply for multiple scholarships, but a combination of multiple scholarships will not be awarded (ESE terms)
documents: Motivation letter (ESSB/ESHCC/ESPhil: max. 1 A4 PDF; ESE: max. 2 A4, Arial 11, covering motivation, evidence of excellence and why the scholarship expands the opportunity to study; ESL: including intended career path)
Budget plan using the EUR template indicating how much money you expect to spend each month (ESSB, ESE, EMC)
CV in PDF format (ESSB, ESHCC, ESL, EMC)
Certified copy of the most recent academic transcript with a wet stamp and signature of a school official - screenshots of online portals are not accepted (ESE)
Certified statement from the educational institution confirming the obtained GPA, using the EUR template or an equivalent statement with the same information (ESE)
Financial statement describing your financial situation and the reason and need to receive the scholarship (ESE, max. 1 A4, Arial 11)
Proof of excellence during the bachelor of laws: certified copy of the bachelor's degree including the grade list (ESL)
selection_criteria: Academic excellence in the previous bachelor programme, with an average grade equivalent to at least 7.50-8.0 on the Dutch 1-10 scale depending on the school
Demonstrated financial need and the extent to which the scholarship enlarges the opportunity to study, shown through the motivation letter and budget plan
The number of applications each year exceeds the number of available scholarships, so no rights can be derived from meeting the minimum application criteria (ESE terms)
At ESHCC the Dean decides on nominations based on the advice of the Scholarship Committee; at ESL an awards committee decides and notifies applicants at the end of May
coverage: Housing, living costs and statutory tuition fee (central Erasmus Trustfonds wording)
Tuition fee waived for both statutory-fee and institutional-fee payers (ESE 2027-2028)
Living allowance of €1.200 per month plus a one-off personal allowance of €249 (ESE 2027-2028)
One year of accommodation in a residence of the Social Hub (TSH Changemaker variant)
Immigration fee of €228 waived, if applicable (ESE 2027-2028)
application_method: Apply for the master programme through Studielink and submit the scholarship application inside the EUR Admissions Portal while applying (ESSB; possible from 1 October onwards); applications submitted by email are not considered (ESHCC)
ESE: submit the scholarship application online via Osiris student once the programme application is in progress; a 'How to apply for a scholarship in Osiris' guide is published by the school
ESL: submit the application by email to the LL.M. Office (informationdesk.llm@law.eur.nl); a (provisional) admission letter from Erasmus School of Law is needed to apply
A scholarship can only be granted after being admitted to the master programme; a conditional offer suffices (ESSB)
official.application_route: Register in Studielink, complete the master application in the EUR Admissions Portal (Osiris student at ESE) and add the scholarship documents in the same portal; ESL applications are emailed to the LL.M. Office.
official.citizenship_residency: Rules vary per school and round: ESHCC's Trustfonds round is for EEA nationals; the ESL Trustfonds and Ter Kulve scholarships are open to individuals from developing countries (World Bank income classification); ESE and ESSB welcome both EEA and non-EEA students; the Erasmus MC round is for non-EEA students only.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. Both EEA and non-EEA students can apply for the Erasmus Trustfonds Scholarship, with nationality rules varying per school. Non-EEA students who qualify for the institutional tuition fee receive a fee waiver covering the difference between the institutional and statutory fee at ESSB and EMC, and a full institutional-fee waiver at ESE for 2027-2028.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants must target a participating master programme at one of the schools offering the scholarship: ESL, ESSB, ESHCC, ESHPM, RSM, ESE, ESPhil or Erasmus MC. ESE's round is limited to Master Accounting, Auditing and Control, Econometrics and Management Science, or Economics and Business; EMC's to the research masters Health Sciences, Neuroscience or Molecular Medicine; ESL's Trustfonds to Commercial Law (and specialisations), International and European Union Law, and Law and Technology.
official.duration: One academic year; if the student fails to graduate in one year, the standard tuition fee applies for the remaining period of study
official.description: The Erasmus Trustfonds was founded to support research and education projects organised by Erasmus University Rotterdam specifically, with the fund aiming to contribute to the growth and flourishing of Erasmus University. Its master's scholarships support high-achieving applicants who are unable to finance their studies themselves, covering housing, living costs and tuition fees for one academic year, with nationalities and procedures varying per school.
official.english_requirement: Programme-specific and published per master programme. For the scholarship-eligible ESE masters: minimum Academic IELTS 6.5; TOEFL iBT 91 total with minimum subscore 22 (old scale) or total 5.0 with minimum subscore 4.5 (new 2026 scale); Cambridge C1 Advanced 176; C2 Proficiency 176 (min. subscore 176, total 180); LanguageCert Academic 65; PTE Academic 65. The test must have been taken within two years of application and scores must be valid before the application deadline. Online English tests are not accepted for visa and residence permit purposes under IND regulations for non-EEA students (IELTS Indicator, IELTS One Skill Retake, TOEFL Home Edition and TOEFL MyBest Scores are excluded); EEA students may use online test versions. Exemptions are only granted for a bachelor or master degree completed in person in Australia, Canada (except Quebec), Ireland, New Zealand, South Africa, the United Kingdom (except commonwealth countries and territories) or the United States, English as a first language during at least 2.5 years of secondary school in those countries, a Dutch VWO diploma with English as an exam subject, or a Dutch four-year HBO diploma including an English language course; an English-taught bachelor degree or IB alone is not sufficient grounds for exemption.

applicant_utility.summary: EUR's flagship master's funding is the Erasmus Trustfonds Scholarship, worth up to €17,500 for one academic year and covering housing, living costs and tuition fees, with the exact structure set by each school. The only round with published dates is ESE's 2027-2028 edition: applications open 1 December 2026 and close 1 February 2027, so candidates should draft their motivation letter, budget plan and certified transcripts during autumn 2026. Selection combines academic excellence (bachelor average of at least 7.5-8.0 on the Dutch scale) with demonstrated financial need, and a scholarship can only be awarded once you are admitted. Applicants from underrepresented groups should also weigh the combined Trustfonds-TSH Changemaker Scholarship, which layers a year of Social Hub housing on top of the funding package.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving, financially constrained applicants to selective EUR master programmes who can document both top grades and genuine funding need.
application_readiness_checklist: Register in Studielink and open your EUR Admissions Portal application early - scholarship documents can be uploaded inside the portal application (ESSB says from 1 October; the ESE master application period opens 1 November 2026)
Get your bachelor transcript and GPA statement certified with a wet stamp and signature now - screenshots and online portal printouts are rejected by ESE
Download EUR's budget plan template and build a realistic monthly budget before writing the motivation letter, since the budget plan is what proves financial need
Book an English test early if you need one: results must be valid before the deadline, can take up to 14 days to publish, and non-EEA visa applicants must test at an official centre
Diary your school's own scholarship deadline (ESE: 1 February 2027; historically 1 April at ESSB, ESHCC, ESPhil and ESL) instead of relying on the programme admission deadline
common_rejection_risks: Missing the scholarship deadline because you assumed it matched the programme admission deadline - they are separate dates at most schools
Uncertified transcripts or GPA statements: ESE requires wet-stamped, signed copies and explicitly rejects screenshots of online portals
Applying at ESE before holding any admission offer - only applicants with an admission offer are considered, although a conditional offer suffices
Trying to stack EUR scholarships: ESE awards only one scholarship type per applicant and will not combine multiple scholarships
Emailing the application where the school mandates the portal - ESHCC states that applications submitted by email will not be considered
Prior enrolment as a full-degree master student in the Netherlands, which excludes you from the ESE round
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Dutch health insurance, any visa and residence-permit costs beyond the waived €228 immigration fee, flights to Rotterdam, and living expenses above the €1,200 monthly allowance are not covered; housing is only guaranteed under the TSH Changemaker variant.
document_audit: Certified copies must carry fresh wet-ink stamps and signatures from a school official or notary - scans of already-stamped documents are not accepted
Motivation letter limits differ per school (1 A4 at ESSB/ESHCC/ESPhil versus 2 A4 Arial 11 at ESE) - check your school's page before drafting
ESE requires both a certified transcript and a separate certified GPA statement on the EUR template or an equivalent home-university statement containing the same information
The budget plan must use EUR's own template and show expected monthly spending; a generic spreadsheet will not satisfy the requirement
English test validity is two years from the test date to your application, and scores must be published before the deadline
alerts: The scholarship and programme deadlines are different dates: at ESE the scholarship closes 1 February 2027 while programme admission for non-EU/EEA applicants runs to 1 April 2027 and EU/EEA to 1 May 2027
ESE states its amount and payment section will be updated in the third week of November 2026 - re-check the breakdown before relying on the €17.500 split
The central Trustfonds page currently shows the 2026-2027 round as closed and directs applicants to the school pages, so monitor your school's scholarship page for the 2027-2028 dates
The funding covers only one academic year; if you do not graduate within that year the standard tuition fee applies for the remainder of the programme
Only one EUR scholarship can be awarded per applicant, so choose the route that fits you best (need-based Trustfonds versus the Changemaker track for underrepresented groups)
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in Studielink, complete the master application in the EUR Admissions Portal (Osiris student at ESE), upload the scholarship documents inside the same application, then await the committee decision by email (ESE: by 13 March 2027; ESSB: before 1 June).
